record.original_question: Is the Kerr black hole nonlinearly stable under perturbations, in the sense that initial data sufficiently close to Kerr evolve back toward a member of the Kerr family rather than toward a qualitatively different spacetime?

evidence.quote: Problem P5: Prove the stability of the Kerr black hole.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\mathcal{M}, g_{a,m})$ denote the Kerr family of stationary, asymptotically flat vacuum solutions of the Einstein vacuum equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ in $3+1$ dimensions, parametrized by mass $m>0$ and angular momentum per unit mass $a$ with $|a| \le m$. Given a smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurface $\Sigma_0$ in a Kerr spacetime with parameters $(a_0, m_0)$, let $(\bar{g}_0, \bar{k}_0)$ be the induced first and second fundamental forms (the initial data set), which satisfy the vacuum constraint equations.

Prove (or disprove) the following nonlinear stability statement: there exists a topology / norm $\|\cdot\|$ on asymptotically flat vacuum initial data on $\Sigma_0$ and an $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every smooth vacuum initial data set $(g, k)$ on $\Sigma_0$ with
$$\|(g - \bar{g}_0,\, k - \bar{k}_0)\| < \varepsilon,$$
the maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum development $(\mathcal{M}, \mathbf{g})$ of $(g,k)$ possesses a complete future null infinity $\mathcal{I}^+$, and the spacetime asymptotically settles down (in the exterior of the event horizon) to a member $g_{a_\infty, m_\infty}$ of the Kerr family with parameters $(a_\infty, m_\infty)$ close to $(a_0, m_0)$, in the sense that suitable geometric quantities measuring the deviation from this Kerr solution decay to zero along $\mathcal{I}^+$ and toward the future event horizon.

Establish this for the entire subextremal Kerr family $|a| < m$ (and address the extremal case $|a|=m$).
artifact.status_search_result: The full nonlinear stability conjecture for the entire subextremal Kerr family remains open. However, substantial progress has been made: Klainerman and Szeftel, together with Giorgi, completed a proof of nonlinear stability of slowly rotating Kerr black holes ($|a|/m \ll 1$) in a series of works culminating in 2022–2023 (e.g., "Kerr stability for small angular momentum", Pure Appl. Math. Quart. 19 (2023)). Linear stability has been established more broadly, including recent 2025 work on linear stability throughout the full subextremal range. The nonlinear case for general $|a|<m$ is still open.

status_evidence.title: Black hole stability conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: In 2022, a series of papers by Giorgi, Klainerman and Szeftel present a proof of the conjecture for slowly rotating Kerr black holes.
status_evidence.claim: Nonlinear stability proved for slowly rotating Kerr; general case still open.

status_evidence.title: Wave equations estimates and the nonlinear stability of slowly rotating Kerr black holes
status_evidence.snippet: Proof of the nonlinear stability of the Kerr family for small angular momentum, i.e |a|/m ≪ 1.
status_evidence.claim: Proven only in the slowly rotating regime.

status_evidence.title: Linear stability of Kerr black holes in the full subextremal range
status_evidence.snippet: Linear stability of Kerr in the full subextremal range.
status_evidence.claim: Linear (not nonlinear) stability extended to full subextremal range.
